questions.question: According to the article, what does the term 'metazoan' refer to?
options: Any member of the group Metazoa
A single-celled organism no longer considered an animal
A member of the clade Bilateria
An organism that produces its own food through photosynthesis
answer_explanations: Correct. The etymology section states that 'A metazoan is any member of the group Metazoa.'
Incorrect. The article states that Protozoa are single-celled organisms no longer considered animals, not metazoans.
Incorrect. While most metazoans may be bilaterians, the article defines metazoan specifically as any member of Metazoa, not exclusively Bilateria.
Incorrect. The article notes that animals cannot produce their own food, unlike plants and algae, so this does not define a metazoan.

questions.question: Based on the article's description of early animal classification, which scientist divided the animal kingdom into Metazoa and Protozoa?
options: Ernst Haeckel
Aristotle
Carl Linnaeus
Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in 1874, Ernst Haeckel divided the animal kingdom into the multicellular Metazoa and the Protozoa.
Incorrect. Aristotle divided animals into those with blood and those without, not into Metazoa and Protozoa.
Incorrect. Carl Linnaeus created the first hierarchical biological classification for animals in 1758 with Systema Naturae.
Incorrect. Jean-Baptiste Lamarck expanded Linnaeus's classification into 14 phyla by 1809.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the blastula and gastrula stages in animal embryonic development as presented in the article?
options: The blastula invaginates to form the gastrula with a digestive chamber and two germ layers
The gastrula develops into a blastula during early embryonic development
The blastula and gastrula are interchangeable terms for the same hollow sphere stage
The gastrula forms directly from the zygote without a preceding blastula stage
answer_explanations: Correct. The reproduction section states that the blastula first invaginates to form a gastrula with a digestive chamber and two separate germ layers.
Incorrect. The article describes the blastula as developing into a gastrula, not the reverse.
Incorrect. The article treats blastula and gastrula as distinct sequential stages, not interchangeable terms.
Incorrect. The article states that zygotes develop into a hollow sphere called a blastula, which then forms the gastrula.

questions.question: If a newly discovered multicellular organism lacks cell walls and instead has cells embedded in an extracellular matrix composed of collagen and elastic glycoproteins, what conclusion about its classification is best supported by the article?
options: It is likely an animal, as these are structural features that set animals apart from all other living things
It is likely a plant or fungus, since these organisms also have extracellular matrices
It cannot be classified without genetic sequencing, as structural features are not diagnostic
It is likely an alga, because algae produce their own food and have flexible cell walls
answer_explanations: Correct. The structural features section states that animals have cells surrounded by an extracellular matrix composed of collagen and elastic glycoproteins, a characteristic that sets them apart from all other living things.
Incorrect. The article contrasts animals with plants and fungi, noting that those organisms have cell walls rather than an extracellular matrix.
Incorrect. The article presents structural features like the extracellular matrix as definitive characteristics that distinguish animals from other multicellular organisms.
Incorrect. The article states that algae produce their own food and are held in place by cell walls, unlike the organism described.

questions.question: According to the article, what is the significance of Hox genes in animal development?
options: They signal the times and places to develop structures such as body segments and limbs
They control the formation of the extracellular matrix in all multicellular organisms
They determine whether an animal reproduces sexually or asexually
They are responsible for producing haploid gametes by meiosis
answer_explanations: Correct. The development section states that development in Bilateria and Cnidaria is controlled by Hox genes, which signal the times and places to develop structures such as body segments and limbs.
Incorrect. The article does not attribute control of extracellular matrix formation to Hox genes.
Incorrect. The article does not link Hox genes to the mode of reproduction.
Incorrect. The article states that haploid gametes are produced by meiosis, not by Hox genes.

questions.question: Based on the article's discussion of evolutionary relationships, what can be inferred about the common ancestor of all living animals?
options: It lived about 650 million years ago during the Cryogenian period
It appeared during the Cambrian explosion around 539 million years ago
It was a bilaterally symmetric organism with a cephalised body plan
It was a single-celled protozoan that later evolved into multicellular Metazoa
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 6,331 groups of genes common to all living animals may have arisen from a single common ancestor that lived about 650 Mya during the Cryogenian period.
Incorrect. The Cambrian explosion is when most modern animal phyla appeared, not when the common ancestor lived.
Incorrect. Bilateral symmetry and cephalisation describe most bilaterians, not necessarily the common ancestor of all living animals.
Incorrect. The article states that Protozoa are single-celled organisms no longer considered animals, and animals arose from a single common ancestor, not from a protozoan.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes the article's explanation of why animals cannot produce their own food?
options: Animals are heterotrophs that ingest organic material and digest it internally
Animals lack chloroplasts and therefore cannot perform photosynthesis
Animals rely on plants and phytoplankton for all of their energy needs
Animals have lost the ability to produce food through evolution
answer_explanations: Correct. The characteristics section states that unlike plants and algae, animals cannot produce their own food, a feature they share with fungi, and that animals ingest organic material and digest it internally.
Incorrect. While true biologically, the article does not mention chloroplasts as the reason animals cannot produce their own food.

Incorrect. The article states most animals rely on biomass and bioenergy produced by plants and phytoplankton, but this is a consequence, not the explanation for why they cannot produce their own food.
Incorrect. The article does not state that animals lost the ability to produce food through evolution.

questions.question: According to the article, what is a likely consequence of repeated mating with a close relative in an animal population?
options: Inbreeding depression due to increased prevalence of harmful recessive traits
Increased genetic diversity and adaptation to the environment
Development of a blastula stage during embryonic development
A shift from sexual to asexual reproduction
answer_explanations: Correct. The reproduction section states that repeated instances of mating with a close relative generally leads to inbreeding depression within a population due to the increased prevalence of harmful recessive traits.
Incorrect. The article states that inbreeding increases harmful recessive traits, which reduces fitness rather than increasing genetic diversity.
Incorrect. The blastula stage is part of normal embryonic development and is not a consequence of inbreeding.
Incorrect. The article discusses asexual reproduction separately and does not link it to inbreeding.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios best applies the article's concept of an evolutionary arms race between predator and prey?
options: A prey species evolves faster running speed, leading the predator species to evolve better camouflage for ambush
A herbivore species shifts from eating grass to eating leaves after a drought kills most grasses
A parasitic wasp lays eggs inside a host, and the host's immune system encapsulates the eggs
A population of insects develops resistance to a pesticide through random mutation and selection
answer_explanations: Correct. The article describes an evolutionary arms race as selective pressures imposed on one another leading to antagonistic coevolution between predator and prey; this scenario shows reciprocal adaptation.
Incorrect. This describes a dietary shift in response to environmental change, not reciprocal selective pressure between predator and prey.
Incorrect. While this is a consumer-resource interaction, the article frames the arms race specifically as reciprocal evolutionary change between predator and prey, not a single defensive response.
Incorrect. This describes evolution in response to a non-living chemical pressure, not the reciprocal coevolution between predator and prey described in the article.

questions.question: Based on the article's description of basal animal phyla, which of the following is one of the five major clades into which the animal kingdom is divided?
options: Porifera
Protozoa
Metazoa
Animalia
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the animal kingdom is divided into five major clades: Porifera, Ctenophora, Placozoa, Cnidaria, and Bilateria.
Incorrect. The article states that Protozoa are single-celled organisms no longer considered animals, not one of the five major clades.
Incorrect. Metazoa is described as synonymous with Animalia, not as one of the five major clades.
Incorrect. Animalia is the biological kingdom itself, not one of the five major clades into which it is divided.
